title: Leasing and sale and lease back
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers leasing or sale and lease back; the closest, financing a new business, is about equity versus debt and is a broader, different idea.

draft.title: Leasing and sale and lease back
card: A business pays regular fees to use an asset it does not own. The lessor (the owner) keeps ownership. The business avoids a large upfront purchase.
A business sells an asset it owns to another party. It then leases the same asset back and keeps using it.
Sale and lease back turns an owned asset into cash, which can be used to pay debts or fund other needs. The cost is regular lease payments from then on.
In both cases the business can use the asset, but the lessor is the one who owns it.
draft.remember: Leasing is paying to use an asset. Sale and lease back sells it for cash, then pays to keep using it.

a.q: Which describes a sale and lease back?
opts: Selling a delivery van, then renting it from the buyer
Renting a delivery van from a dealer instead of buying it
Buying a delivery van with a loan from a bank
Buying a second delivery van and renting out the first
a.why: In a sale and lease back the business first owns the asset, sells it, then rents it back. Simply renting a van from a dealer is leasing, but the business never owned the van, so no sale takes place.
a.clue: The business must own the asset first.

b.q: Priya owns the building that houses her bakery in Orange. She needs cash to pay off a short-term debt but wants to keep baking there. Which strategy suits her?
opts: Sell the building and lease it back from the buyer
Lease a second building from another owner
Keep the building and lease out her ovens
Buy new ovens and lease them to another bakery
b.why: Selling the building gives Priya cash, and leasing it back lets her keep using it. Leasing a second building only adds a cost and brings in no cash, because she would be paying fees without selling anything.
b.clue: She needs cash from an asset she already owns.

a.best: Selling a delivery van, then renting it from the buyer

b.best: Sell the building and lease it back from the buyer
